data.narrative:
Electric Air, a Seed-stage Climate & Energy company founded by Chris Mui and Jeremy Osbourne, is evaluated against a sector universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (Linazo, LNZA). The company has raised $500K to date with an undisclosed valuation.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable triangulation lens. Using total raised ($500K) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.5x Seed-to-next-stage multiplier yields an implied valuation of $1.25M. The Peer-Median method could not be reliably applied; while 8 same-sector peers exist in the Climate & Energy space (including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix), none satisfied minimum threshold criteria for narrow-filter comparability (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier), requiring at least three datapoints for statistical validity.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.06M to $1.44M, with a median of $1.25M. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single method and highlights material uncertainty: the absence of directly comparable Seed-stage Climate & Energy transactions limits confidence in the step-up multiplier. Key risks to valuation include stage-progression assumptions specific to this sector and the early-stage nature of available comparable data. Investors should treat this as an indicative floor pending acquisition of more granular peer transaction data or advancement of company milestones.
